content: Numerous randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have assessed the effectiveness of real-time continuous glucose monitoring (rtCGM) across various patient populations. These studies demonstrate that rtCGM significantly reduces hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) levels, particularly in individuals undergoing insulin therapy. Additionally, rtCGM has been shown to decrease both the duration and frequency of hypoglycemic episodes. Research indicates that rtCGM is effective in improving glycemic control in both younger and older adults. Specifically, it enhances time in range (TIR), which refers to the proportion of time blood glucose levels remain within the desired target range, thereby reducing the occurrence of both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia.
